editorial:
You know that feeling when your best friend suddenly becomes the enemy? That is exactly where Nadine finds herself in this sharp, funny coming-of-age story. She is a sarcastic, awkward high school junior who has always leaned on her one true friend, Krista. When Krista starts dating Nadine's popular older brother Darian, Nadine feels completely betrayed and spirals into a mess of bad decisions, dramatic outbursts, and lonely lunches. The movie nails that raw teenage feeling of being left behind while everyone else seems to have life figured out. Hailee Steinfeld carries the whole thing with a performance that is both hilarious and heartbreaking, and Woody Harrelson steals scenes as her dry, no-nonsense teacher who somehow becomes her unlikely anchor.

The pacing is quick and the dialogue feels real, like actual teenagers talking instead of movie teenagers. The humor lands without trying too hard, and the emotional beats hit harder because the characters feel so genuine. On the downside, Nadine can be frustratingly self-centered, which might test your patience, and some side characters do not get enough screen time. Still, if you enjoy smart teen comedies with heart, this one is a gem. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: After pushing everyone away, Nadine finally hits rock bottom and realizes she has been unfair to Krista and Darian. She apologizes to both, admitting her jealousy and selfishness. She also lets go of her crush on the wrong guy and accepts that Erwin, the sweet classmate she kept ignoring, actually cares about her. The final scene shows Nadine attending Erwin's animated film screening, where they hold hands and share a quiet, hopeful moment. It is not a fairy-tale fix, but a realistic step toward growing up and letting people in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart teen comedies with real heart and relatable characters.
